item.title: [Feature Request] Show source location for custom prompts and skills in the prompt picker (parity with agents)
item.body:
## Problem

Custom agents (`.agent.md`) show an **edit icon** in the picker, making it easy to identify their source and jump to the definition file. However, **custom prompts** (`.prompt.md`) and **skills** (`.github/skills/*/SKILL.md`) displayed in the prompt picker provide **no indication of where they are defined**.

This makes it very difficult to:
1. Determine whether a prompt comes from the **workspace** (`.github/prompts/`), **user global** (`~/.vscode/prompts/`), or **skills** (`.github/skills/`)
2. Navigate to the source file to edit or review it
3. Debug unexpected or duplicate prompt entries

### Current behavior

**Agents** — The agent picker shows an edit (pencil) icon next to each agent. Clicking it opens the `.agent.md` source file. This is great UX.

**Prompts/Skills** — The prompt picker lists all prompts and skills as flat slash commands (e.g., `/code-simplifier`, `/export-knowledge`, `/azure-env-builder`) with only a description. There is **no visual indicator** of:
- Source type (workspace prompt vs. user prompt vs. skill)
- Source file path
- Any way to navigate to the definition

### Expected behavior

Prompts and skills in the picker should have **source visibility parity** with agents. Suggested improvements (any combination would help):

1. **Edit icon** — Show the same pencil icon that agents have, opening the source `.prompt.md` or `SKILL.md` on click
2. **Source badge/label** — Display a small label like `workspace`, `user`, or `skill` next to each entry
3. **Tooltip with path** — Show the source file path on hover (e.g., `.github/skills/code-simplifier/SKILL.md`)
4. **"Go to Definition"** — Right-click context menu to open the source file

## Why this matters

As the number of prompts and skills grows (workspace prompts + user global prompts + skills from `.github/skills/`), the picker becomes a flat list with no way to distinguish entries. Users cannot tell:
- Why a certain slash command appeared
- Which file to edit to modify its behavior
- Whether it's a workspace-level or user-level prompt

This is especially confusing when skills (`SKILL.md`) appear alongside traditional prompts (`.prompt.md`) with identical UX treatment.

## Environment

- VS Code: 1.109.3
- GitHub Copilot Chat: 0.37.6
- OS: Windows 11
